blocks.content: Imagine yourself at the gateway to scenic beauty, where the majestic Kangra and Dalhousie foothills embrace you in their natural splendour. Welcome to Pathankot, a bustling city that beckons you to explore the enchanting realms of Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh. Here, the Beas and Ravi rivers serenade you with their tranquil whispers, weaving a lush green landscape adorned with ancient forts and temples steeped in history.

Pathankot is both the end of a road and the beginning as the national highway that stretches up to the northern hills culminates here. The city also shares borders with three states of Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir and Punjab. Often used as a rest stop by many travellers and trekking enthusiasts, the land welcomes you with open arms. Lose yourself in its bustling markets, where colours and aromas dance in harmony, or simply unwind by the riverside, soaking in the serenity of nature's embrace. Pathankot is a city that promises an unforgettable experience, inviting you to become a part of its rich life and history.
Witness the divine presence of ancient temples and sacred shrines in Pathankot that beckons you to embark on a soul-stirring journey.

Begin your journey at Ashapurni Mandir, dedicated to the goddess of fulfilment. As you step into its hallowed precincts, the scent of incense lingering in the air will fill your senses and the sound of devotees' prayers dances in your mind. Marvel at the intricate architecture and the idol of the goddess, radiating divine grace. Next, visit Baba Murad Shah Dargah, a revered Sufi shrine that exudes peace and tranquillity. Picture the majestic domes and minarets, the white marble reflecting the sunlight, and the devotees, their faces aglow with devotion, paying homage to the Sufi saint. It is believed that Pathankot was established by the first Sikh Guru – Guru Nanak Dev Ji. So, don't miss visiting Gurdwara Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji and Gurdwara Shri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji where their teachings come alive in peaceful ambience. Experience the profound sense of community and service as you participate in the langar, a sacred tradition of serving free meals to all, regardless of caste, creed, or status. Let the hymns of the Guru Granth Sahib uplift your spirit and fill your heart with divine bliss. Another spiritual abode to seek blessings is the Kali Mata Ka Mandir, a temple dedicated to the fierce goddess Kali. Here, feel the idol of the goddess, with her multiple arms symbolising power and protection, towering over you as the devotees offer their prayers. Explore the spiritual haven of Radha Krishna Mandir, where the divine love of Radha and Krishna is celebrated. Always adorned with colourful decorations, the temple atmosphere is filled with melodious bhajans. Delve into the spiritual realm at Kathgarh Temple, an ancient shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva. Witness the intricate carvings and architectural splendour of this temple, which is believed to date back to the Mahabharata era. Discover the mystical Nagni Temple, dedicated to the serpent deity Nagni Devi. This centuries-old temple is revered for its unique architecture and spiritual significance, drawing devotees from far and wide seeking blessings and protection. Your journey is set to take a surprising turn with a visit to Mukteshwar Temple, a mesmerising cave temple! Conclude your spiritual tour of Pathankot at Shri Laxmi Narayan Mandir, where the divine couple, Lord Vishnu and Goddess Lakshmi, are believed to reside.

Pathankot’s architectural brilliance is reflected not just in its spiritual sites but its awe-striking forts as well. The Shahpur Kandi Fort, for example, is a symbol of Rajput strength and resilience, standing proudly against the test of time. Marvel at its imposing walls and strategic location, offering panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. Another trip into the city’s history can be made through the enchanting Nurpur Fort, named after the Mughal empress Nur Jahan, a masterpiece of Mughal architecture. Feel the historical presence as you wander through its ancient corridors and courtyards, imagining life in the royal Rajputi courts.

Whether you are a nature enthusiast or not, you are sure to be inspired by the land’s conservation efforts. Begin your journey at the Dhar Nature Retreat and Awareness Camp and explore its unspoiled forest. The retreat is also home to Ranjit Sagar Lake where breathtaking landscapes and abundant biodiversity await. Trek through the lush green hills where the melodies of birds and the rustling leaves create a symphony you will never forget. Continue your adventure at the Kathlour Kushlian Wildlife Sanctuary , a haven for wildlife enthusiasts. Discover a variety of plant species, from towering trees to delicate flowers, each contributing to the sanctuary's rich biodiversity. Keep a lookout for the its residents - leopards, langurs, and a myriad of bird species, as they go about their daily routines in this natural paradise!

Pathankot's Punjabi cuisine, a true reflection of its rich cultural heritage, will offer you a delightful blend of flavours that will leave you wanting to come back for more. Begin your culinary adventure with a classic Punjabi breakfast of aloo puri at any local eatery. Dive into the chole bhature, a local favourite and a must-try for visitors. Explore the vibrant street food scene and treat yourself to golgappas, or indulge in sarson da saag with makki di roti at a local dhaba. For a sweet end to your culinary journey, drive to the nearby Lakhanpur and relish the mouth-watering ‘Lakhanpur ke Bhalle’ served with spicy radish chutney. You should surely pay a visit to locally renowned eateries like Pind Balluchi or Mama’s Rasoi, which serve authentic Punjabi flavours.

As you bid farewell to Pathankot, continue your exploration with nearby prominent hill stations like Dharamshala and Dalhousie . Pathankot is nothing short of paradise during the winter months (Oct - Mar). If you wish to experience the city in its most glorious form, plan your trip around the Baisakhi and Lohri festivals that take place during the months of January and April. These times will leave an unforgettable picture of unity and grandeur that you will cherish for years to come. With its rich history, diverse cuisine, and natural beauty, Pathankot will leave an indelible mark on your journey.
Legend has it that the Pandavas from the epic Mahabharata stayed at the Mukteshwar Temple during their exile.
